author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)

months.note: 국내에서는 9~10월에 보이며, 번식지에서는 5월 중순~하순에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 우리나라에서는 9~10월에 적은 무리가 지나가는 나그네새로, 바닷가 간석지나 습지에서 지낸다. 주로 곤충을 먹고 조개류, 갑각류, 환형동물과 식물 열매도 먹는다. 구북구 북부에서 번식하며 풀밭이나 관목이 있는 땅에 접시 모양 둥지를 짓고 알을 4개쯤 낳는다. 겨울은 아프리카와 아시아의 온대·열대 지역에서 난다.

art.subject: Ruff (Calidris pugnax), adult male in non-breeding plumage, as seen on Korean tidal flats and wetlands in September: head and neck plain pale grey-brown with whitish feathering around the bill base and on the throat; mantle, scapulars and wing coverts grey-brown with dark centres and neat pale fringes, giving a scaly look; breast lightly washed grey-brown; belly and undertail white. Bill dark, short and slightly drooping; dark eye; legs dull orange-yellow.
art.pose: walking on a tidal flat, picking up insects
art.scene: Korean autumn: coastal tidal flat and adjoining wetland in September; no people, buildings or text
views: adult non-breeding (September), side view standing: scaly grey-brown upperparts with pale fringes, plain grey-brown head and neck, whitish around the bill base, white underparts with a grey-brown breast wash, short slightly drooping dark bill, orange-yellow legs

adult male breeding (May), side view standing: large erectile ruff of neck feathers and short ear tufts, white, purplish-black or chestnut depending on the individual, bare warty facial skin, orange legs
in flight, seen from above: grey-brown upperparts, narrow white wing-bar, dark rump centre flanked by two white oval patches
art.build: Medium-sized, pot-bellied sandpiper with a strong size difference between the sexes: male about 32cm, larger than a Common Redshank, female about 25cm. Small head on a longish neck, upright stance with a slightly humped back. Bill about head length or shorter, slightly drooping at the tip. Legs fairly long, their colour varying from greenish-yellow to orange. In flight a narrow white wing-bar and two white oval patches on either side of a dark rump and tail centre.
avoid: Do not show the ruff or ear tufts on the non-breeding bird; they occur only on breeding males in spring.
Do not paint a long, fine bill; the Ruff's bill is short, about head length, and slightly drooping.
Do not paint a fully white rump; the white is in two oval patches on either side of a dark centre.
Do not make males and females the same size; the male is much larger.
